decision: how to tell a new conflict from a failed update
choice: a dirty PR after a ready is not a failure when another ticket of the repo entered merged at or after the update job was queued (ticket_transitions)
why: TrackedTicket carries no base sha and the ticket names only merge_queue.py; every factory merge already writes a merged transition with the queue clock, and a merge after the job was queued may be missing from the main it merged. An untracked hand merge to main is not seen, so that rare case still counts once

decision: what happens to the new conflict
choice: back to merge-queue with update_from_head cleared and update_failures unchanged; the same poll's queue pass queues one more update
why: reuses the existing updating -> merge-queue edge (update-failed-1 already takes it), so the statechart and model need no new edge

choice: an entry that may share files with the waiting head passes it only while no other ticket merged since the head's approved_at (MERGES_BEFORE_OVERLAP_WAITS = 1); entries with disjoint changed_files always pass
why: the ticket offers overlap or a cap; overlap alone needs changed_files, which is read only on hold repos, so unknown files fail closed to the cap. The count comes from durable ticket_transitions, so a poller restart grants no extra pass and no new column is needed

decision: count disjoint merges toward the cap
why: which merged PRs were disjoint is not recorded; over-counting only makes an overlapping entry wait sooner, never lets the head be passed twice
